newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares shrug off weak start, end steady.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares shrug off weak start, end steady.

text.p: Austrian shares recovered lost ground on Thursday to end virtually unchanged and market participants said the ATX index had found a floor, pointing to an uneventful expiry of February futures on Friday.
The ATX index of 21 blue-chip shares closed 0.65 points down at 1,213.10, having rebounded off a session low of 1,206.74. February ATX futures stood 2.7 down at 1,211.4.
"I don't expect any fireworks ahead of the expiry tomorrow. Most people have already rolled forward their positions," a trader said.

Eight ATX shares closed higher, 11 lower and two unchanged. Activity centred on oil and chemicals group OMV and steelmaker VA Stahl, which ended a volatile session at a new closing high of 472.55 schillings.
VA Stahl dipped to 452 schillings early on, then rebounded to an intra-day high of 475. It was the day's biggest percentage gainer, up 1.62 percent.
"At the start there was one very aggressive seller in VA Stahl but then the buyers came out in force," a trader said.

Motorcycle manufacturer KTM was the biggest decliner, down 3.65 percent to 739 schillings as investors took profits out of a recent rally. Semi-conductor maker AMS also eased on profit-taking, down 31 schillings to 1,209.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index finished 0.21 points up at 450.26. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 254
